design_detail: Cross-sectional postpartum depression screening study (authors call it a sequential case series), single urban US academic hospital; telephone EPDS at 4–6 weeks postpartum with SCID home diagnostic interviews for screen-positive women; descriptive proportions and χ2/Fisher tests only
severity_measure: No adjustment of any kind; purely descriptive (EPDS used only as the screening/eligibility threshold)
comparison_group: None (descriptive); crude demographic comparison of screen-positive vs screen-negative women
population: Postpartum women (≥18 y, English-speaking) with live births at Magee-Womens Hospital, Pittsburgh, screened 4–6 weeks after delivery
sample_size_detail: 826 screen-positive women completed home SCID evaluation (basis for onset-timing and diagnosis estimates). Source: 17,601 approached, 17,426 eligible, 13,442 contacted, 10,000 screened; 1396 screen-positive (EPDS ≥10); 147 completed a telephone MDD interview only. Self-harm ideation rates reported for all 10,000 screened and for the 1396 screen-positive.
rationale: Screening program with descriptive diagnostic characterization; no exposure–outcome effect estimate and no adjustment. The headline findings (onset timing, primary/secondary DSM-IV diagnoses) rest on the 826 SCID-assessed women; the 10,000 screened are the broader descriptive sample.

design_detail: Planned secondary analysis of a prospective cohort (EHR abstraction) comparing pre- vs post-implementation epochs of a perinatal collaborative care model at one US academic center; multivariable logistic regression with propensity-score covariate adjustment and race-by-epoch interaction terms; no concurrent non-implementing control
severity_measure: Propensity score: maternal age, insurance, parity, tobacco, substance-use history, chronic medical problem, any mental health history (presence only); postpartum models added GDM and preterm birth. No depression-severity measure.
comparison_group: Pre-implementation epoch (deliveries 2015–2016) vs post-implementation (2017–2019); White individuals as referent for race contrasts
population: Pregnant/postpartum people self-identified as Black or White receiving prenatal care at Northwestern Medicine (Chicago) collaborative-care-affiliated obstetric practices
sample_size_detail: 4710 individuals delivering ≥20 weeks: 575 Black, 4135 White; pre-implementation 2286 (262 Black/2024 White), post-implementation 2424 (313 Black/2111 White). Treatment-recommendation outcome analyzed only among screen-positive women (pre: 17 Black/9 White; post: 41 Black/89 White).
rationale: Before/after comparison of implementation epochs without a concurrent control, so per protocol not quasi-experimental; estimates are propensity-score adjusted. Adjustment includes only presence of a mental health history, not severity. Primary outcome (antenatal screening) modeled in all 4710.

design_detail: Statewide population-based descriptive study (authors: case series) of pregnancy-associated deaths from suicide or accidental overdose identified through Colorado maternal mortality surveillance (death/birth certificate linkage, MMRC review); medical/coroner record abstraction; frequencies and death ratios per 100,000 live births, with crude contextual comparison to all Colorado live births
severity_measure: No adjustment; descriptive frequencies and mortality ratios only
comparison_group: None formal; descriptive context comparison with all women with live births in Colorado 2004–2012 (n=614,154)
population: Women with pregnancy-associated deaths (during pregnancy or within 1 year postpartum) from suicide or accidental overdose, Colorado, 2004–2012
sample_size_detail: 59 self-harm decedents with detailed records (31 accidental overdose, 28 suicide) of 63 self-harm deaths among 211 pregnancy-associated deaths; toxicology available for 50; prenatal records for 48. Contextual comparison: 614,154 women with live births.
rationale: Descriptive surveillance analysis with no adjusted comparison. Coded descriptive rather than case series because the cases are outcome cases (deaths) from population-based surveillance with death ratios and a crude live-birth comparison, and code 5 precedes code 9. Main descriptive estimates rest on the 59 women with records.

design_detail: Prospective cohort (subgroup with prior depressive disorder) from a multisite obstetric-practice cohort in Connecticut/western Massachusetts; CIDI interviews twice in pregnancy and once postpartum; Cox regression with time-dependent, 2-month-lagged antidepressant use, adjusted for prespecified confounders
severity_measure: Number of prior depressive episodes (1, 2, 3, ≥4), depression onset before age 14, number of prior hospitalizations for depression, and major depressive episode in the 6 months before pregnancy
comparison_group: Pregnant women with a history of depression not using antidepressants (time-varying exposure)
population: Pregnant women with a history of depressive disorder recruited before 17 weeks from 137 obstetric practices/clinics in CT and western MA, pregnancies 2005–2009
sample_size_detail: Analytic sample 778 women with prior depressive disorder and no MDE in pregnancy month 1 (from 9525 screened, 3517 invited, 2793 interviewed). 130 women used antidepressants during the study period; 123 developed an MDE; 617 completed both follow-up interviews.
rationale: Non-randomized comparison of antidepressant users vs nonusers (adjusted HR 0.88). Adjustment set explicitly includes episode count, early onset, prior hospitalization and recent MDE, described as 'correlates of severe depressive illness'.

design_detail: Retrospective cohort nested in US Medicaid Analytic eXtract 2000–2010; main analysis restricted to women with a depression diagnosis with high-dimensional propensity-score stratification (100 strata); logistic regression; separate models per antidepressant class
severity_measure: Proxies for depression severity: number of outpatient and inpatient depression diagnoses; plus other psychotropic use (antipsychotics, anticonvulsants, lithium, benzodiazepines, etc.) and healthcare-use markers
comparison_group: Pregnant women with depression and no antidepressant use during pregnancy
population: Pregnant women in US Medicaid (46 states + DC) with live births, 2000–2010; main analysis restricted to women with depression
sample_size_detail: Main estimate (SSRI vs unexposed, depression-restricted, hdPS-stratified OR 1.10): 65,316 SSRI-exposed + 657,515 unexposed. Non-SSRI contrast: 16,283 + 657,515 = 673,798. Full depression-restricted cohort 739,114. Source cohort 3,789,330 eligible pregnancies (102,179 SSRI, 26,771 non-SSRI, 3,660,380 unexposed).
rationale: Depression restriction plus PS/hdPS adjustment with covariates explicitly labeled 'proxies for depression severity'. N is the SSRI contrast (headline estimate; classes had separate PS models); the full depression-restricted cohort would be 739,114.

design_detail: Secondary analysis of two prospective observational pregnancy cohorts (Cleveland OH, Pittsburgh PA); infants examined with a modified Finnegan scale at 2–4 weeks by raters blind to exposure; χ2/Kruskal-Wallis group comparisons plus multivariable logistic regression
severity_measure: Logistic model adjusted for preterm birth, maternal race and age only; maternal SIGH-ADS depression scores compared descriptively but not entered in the Finnegan-sign model
comparison_group: Infants of women with untreated mood disorder (MDD or bipolar) and infants of women with neither mood disorder nor psychotropic use
population: Pregnant women with MDD/bipolar disorder (SRI-treated or untreated) or no mood disorder, and their infants, enrolled 2000–2011 in Cleveland and Pittsburgh
sample_size_detail: 41 SRI-exposed, 94 untreated mood disorder, 79 comparison; no attrition from the analyzed sample reported.
rationale: Headline results are crude sign rates (34.1% vs 35.1% vs 30.4%), but the paper reports an adjusted logistic model (preterm birth, race, age; results not shown) for the exposure–outcome association, which governs under Amendment 2. No severity measure in that model; grouping by mood-disorder diagnosis alone does not count.

design_detail: Single-center, 6-week double-blind placebo-controlled RCT of flexible-dose sertraline (50–200 mg/day) after a 1-week single-blind placebo lead-in; primary analysis χ2 comparison of response rates in ITT sample
population: Women aged 18–45 with major depression onset within 3 months postpartum (infant <12 months), recruited in New Haven/southern Connecticut, 1994–2004
sample_size_detail: 38 entered placebo lead-in; 2 removed for >30% HAM-D improvement; 36 randomized (17 sertraline, 19 placebo) = ITT; 33 evaluable (≥3 post-randomization assessments); 27 met strict DSM-IV 4-week onset criterion.
rationale: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial in postpartum depression; N is the number randomized (36).

design_detail: Systematic review and random-effects network meta-analysis (credible intervals) of randomised placebo- and active-controlled drug trials for generalised anxiety disorder; PROSPERO CRD42018087106
comparison_group: Placebo and other active drugs (22 active drugs in network)
population: Adult outpatients with generalised anxiety disorder in randomised trials published 1994–2017 (not perinatal)
sample_size_detail: 89 RCTs randomizing 25,441 patients to 22 active drugs or placebo; 1992 potential studies screened; includes 16 trials conducted in China.
rationale: Network meta-analysis restricted to randomised clinical trials; counts consistent between abstract and extracted full text (PDF text partly garbled).

design_detail: Two-part study: literature review of 8 cohort studies to generate hypotheses, then population-based case–malformed-control study in the EUROCAT Antiepileptic Study Database (19 European registries, 1995–2005); logistic regression adjusted for maternal age, birth year, and registry
severity_measure: Adjusted only for maternal age, year of birth and reporting registry; authors state no data on epilepsy type, seizure frequency, folic acid, or dose
comparison_group: No antiepileptic drug exposure (also valproic acid and other AED monotherapy); controls = non-chromosomal malformations (control 1) and chromosomal syndromes (control 2)
population: Malformed live births, fetal deaths ≥20 weeks and terminations in 19 EUROCAT population-based congenital anomaly registries, Europe 1995–2005 (3.88 million births)
sample_size_detail: Case-control sample: 11,790 cases in 5 malformation groups (spina bifida n=2048, 8 carbamazepine-exposed) + 69,883 non-chromosomal controls + 11,763 chromosomal controls = 93,436 registrations; 131 carbamazepine-monotherapy registrations. Source: 98,075 malformation registrations among 3,881,592 births. Literature component: 8 cohorts, 2680 carbamazepine-exposed pregnancies.
rationale: Primary effect estimates (e.g., spina bifida OR 2.6) come from the adjusted case-control analysis; the literature review only generated hypotheses, so coded observational rather than systematic review. Epilepsy severity (seizure type/frequency) was unavailable.

design_detail: Retrospective population-based cohort/prevalence study in MEPREP (11 US health plans incl. Tennessee Medicaid) linked to birth certificates; prevalence and temporal trends of antipsychotic dispensing by year, trimester and diagnosis; descriptive only
comparison_group: None (descriptive); characteristics of exposed vs unexposed deliveries tabulated crudely
population: Live-born deliveries to women aged 15–45 continuously enrolled in 11 US health plans (MEPREP), 2001–2007
sample_size_detail: 4223 deliveries exposed to atypical and 548 to typical antipsychotics (60 days pre-pregnancy through delivery); 514,782 with no antipsychotic use; 68,946 typical-exposed if prochlorperazine/promethazine counted.
rationale: Purely descriptive prevalence and trend analysis with no comparative effect estimate or adjustment.

design_detail: Prospective observational cohort of pregnant women with bipolar disorder (psychotropic-treated or untreated) plus controls from a parallel study; infant BSID-II at 12, 26, 52 weeks; repeated-measures mixed models: Model I unadjusted, Model II adds maternal SIGH-ADS and MRS, Model III adds selected confounders
severity_measure: Maternal depression (SIGH-ADS) and mania (Mania Rating Scale) symptom-severity scores in Models II–III; Model III also maternal age, university education, marital status where indicated
comparison_group: Infants of women with untreated bipolar disorder (BD−) and of women without bipolar disorder or psychotropic exposure
population: Pregnant women with DSM-IV bipolar I/II/NOS and control women, and their infants, Pittsburgh PA, recruited 2006–2011
sample_size_detail: 54 BD+ (psychotropic-treated), 27 BD− (untreated), 116 unexposed controls; per-timepoint assessments fewer (e.g., 52-week MDI: 96/28/20).
rationale: The headline motor-quality effect is from unadjusted Model I and lost significance after adjustment; under Amendment 2 the fully adjusted models govern, and these include symptom-severity scores (SIGH-ADS, MRS).

design_detail: Systematic review and meta-analysis (MOOSE/PRISMA) of metabolic syndrome prevalence; random-effects pooling, relative-risk meta-analyses and meta-regression; file text is the Spanish-language edition PDF
comparison_group: Between diagnostic groups; antipsychotic-treated vs antipsychotic-naïve; matched general-population controls
population: Adults with schizophrenia/related psychotic disorders, bipolar disorder or major depressive disorder (not perinatal)
sample_size_detail: 198 studies, 52,678 unique people with severe mental illness (study sizes 14–3568); 429 publications reviewed.
rationale: Systematic review/meta-analysis of prevalence. Inclusion targeted observational studies (cross-sectional, retrospective, prospective) and baseline data were extracted from RCTs, hence 'Mixed'; not a perinatal population.

design_detail: Retrospective cohort nested in US Medicaid Analytic eXtract 2000–2007; depression-restricted cohort with propensity-score stratification (100 strata), hdPS confirmatory; logistic regression; separate models per antidepressant class
severity_measure: Proxies for depression severity: number of outpatient and inpatient depression diagnoses; plus other psychotropic use and number of distinct prescription drugs
comparison_group: Women with depression and no antidepressant use in the first trimester
population: Pregnant women in US Medicaid (46 states + DC) with live births, 2000–2007; main analysis restricted to women with depression
sample_size_detail: Main estimate (SSRI vs unexposed, depression-restricted PS-stratified RR 1.06): 36,778 SSRI-exposed + 180,564 unexposed. Source cohort 949,504 pregnancies (64,389 first-trimester antidepressant-exposed incl. 46,144 SSRI; 885,115 unexposed).
rationale: Depression restriction plus PS stratification on covariates explicitly described as proxies for depression severity; fully adjusted SSRI contrast is the primary estimate.

design_detail: Retrospective cohort in US Medicaid Analytic eXtract 2000–2007 restricted to women with depression; GEE relative risks adjusted for preeclampsia risk factors, depression-severity proxies, other indications, medications and healthcare use; robust variance for repeat pregnancies
severity_measure: Depression-severity proxies: number of outpatient (0, 1, 2–4, 5–9, ≥10) and inpatient (0, 1, ≥2) depression diagnoses; also anticonvulsant and benzodiazepine dispensing
comparison_group: Women with depression and no antidepressant dispensing (SSRI monotherapy also used as active comparator)
population: Pregnant women with depression diagnoses in US Medicaid (MAX), live-birth deliveries 2000–2007
sample_size_detail: Primary analysis: 59,219 unexposed, 19,000 SSRI, 1216 SNRI, 441 tricyclic, 2622 bupropion, 647 other monotherapy, 2622 polytherapy. Depression cohort 100,942 minus 15,175 with first-trimester-only antidepressant use; source 1,248,875 pregnancies from 1,072,352 women.
rationale: Depression-restricted cohort with full adjustment that includes counts of outpatient and inpatient depression diagnoses, explicitly termed severity proxies. N summed from Table 2 groups.

design_detail: Retrospective cohort in Kaiser Permanente Washington linked to state birth records, 2001–2014; restricted to pre-pregnancy antidepressant users; continuers vs discontinuers; GEE with inverse probability of treatment weighting
severity_measure: IPTW included psychotherapy visits, psychiatry visits and inpatient psychiatric hospitalization in the prior year and psychotropic fills (antipsychotic, benzodiazepine, mood stabilizer), termed 'indicators of mental health severity'; PHQ-9 described but not modeled
comparison_group: Women with antidepressant fills before pregnancy who discontinued (no fill during pregnancy)
population: Singleton live births 2001–2014 to women aged 15–45 enrolled in Kaiser Permanente Washington with an antidepressant fill in the 6 months before pregnancy
sample_size_detail: 1634 continuers, 1211 discontinuers; about 4% with missing covariates excluded from regression (complete-case N not reported). Blood-glucose analysis subset 1101 (613/488).
rationale: Active-comparator design among prior users with IPTW on mental-healthcare utilization, psychiatric hospitalization and psychotropic use as severity indicators. Exact complete-case N for the main IPTW RR is not given, so the eligible 2845 is reported.

design_detail: Retrospective cohort in US Medicaid Analytic eXtract 2000–2007 restricted to women with mood/anxiety disorders; GEE relative risks adjusted for PPH risk factors, severity proxies, other indications and drugs; hdPS sensitivity analysis
severity_measure: Proxies of mood/anxiety disorder severity: number of outpatient (0, 1, 2–5, 6–9, ≥10) and inpatient (0, 1, ≥2) mood/anxiety diagnoses; also anticonvulsant/benzodiazepine use and baseline days in hospital
comparison_group: Women with mood/anxiety disorder and no antidepressant supply in the 5 months before delivery
population: Pregnant women aged 12–55 with mood/anxiety disorder diagnoses in US Medicaid (MAX), live-birth deliveries 2000–2007
sample_size_detail: Primary analysis: 69,044 unexposed; 29,222 SRI monotherapy (12,710 current, 6096 recent, 10,416 past); 4456 non-SRI monotherapy (1495/829/2132). 3278 polytherapy users excluded from the 106,000 mood/anxiety subcohort; source 2,759,414 pregnancies from 2,340,631 women.
rationale: Restriction to mood/anxiety disorders plus adjustment for counts of outpatient and inpatient diagnoses, labeled 'proxies of mood/anxiety disorder severity'. N = Table 1 exposure groups.
